name: Pelvic Tilt (Cat/Cow)

execution.note: Focus on the tucking of the tailbone.

instructions: Step 1: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Step 2: Inhale, drop your belly toward the floor, and look up slightly (Cow).
Step 3: Exhale, round your spine toward the ceiling, and tuck your chin to your chest (Cat).
Step 4: Move rhythmically with your breath.

variations.name: Evening Pelvic Release Shake
variations.instruction_note: A loose, shaking movement on all fours to release evening tension.

variations.name: Quick Prep 8-Rep
variations.instruction_note: Perform exactly 8 reps as part of a 5-minute daily routine.

variations.name: Deep Belly Breath Focus
variations.instruction_note: Emphasize expanding the belly fully on the inhale.

variations.name: Feet In/Out Modification
variations.instruction_note: Experiment with bringing feet together or wide to change pelvic sensations.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Very safe. If wrists are sore, perform on fists instead.
safety_profile.contraindications: None.

enrichment.benefits: Helps baby move into the optimal position (LOA) and relieves back pressure.

name: Forward-Leaning Inversion

execution.note: Hold for exactly 30 seconds.

instructions: Step 1: Kneel on the edge of a couch or stable chair.
Step 2: Carefully lower your hands to the floor one at a time, then lower onto your forearms.
Step 3: Let your head hang freely, tucking your chin slightly to create space in the neck.
Step 4: Keep your knees on the edge of the couch and hips high.
Step 5: To come out, crawl your hands back up to a kneeling position slowly.

variations.name: Doula Optimization Protocol
variations.instruction_note: Immediately follow the inversion with a period of rest or a gentle walk to help the baby settle into the newly created space.

variations.name: 3rd Trimester Low-Impact Version
variations.instruction_note: A slightly modified angle for very late pregnancy comfort.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Always have someone nearby for balance if you feel unsteady. Come up very slowly to prevent a head rush.
safety_profile.contraindications: High blood pressure, history of stroke, glaucoma, or if baby is already in a perfect position and you are in active labor.

enrichment.benefits: Uses gravity to stretch the uterosacral ligaments, giving the baby more room to rotate into the optimal head-down position.

name: Hug the Baby (Pregnant Cat)

execution.note: Focus on the quality of the contraction rather than speed.

instructions: Step 1: Start on hands and knees with a neutral, flat spine.
Step 2: On the inhale, allow your stomach to expand fully toward the floor.
Step 3: On the exhale, blow all the air out and 'hug' your baby in and up toward your spine.
Step 4: Maintain a flat back; do not round your shoulders or tuck your tailbone.
Step 5: Feel the engagement of your deep transverse abdominis and your pelvic floor.

variations.name: Deep Belly Breathes
variations.instruction_note: Focus specifically on the diaphragmatic expansion to relax the pelvic floor on the inhale.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Ensure you are not holding your breath. The engagement happens on the active exhale.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop if you notice 'coning' or 'doming' along the center of your abdomen.

enrichment.benefits: Strengthens the transverse abdominis to support the weight of the belly and stabilize the spine.

name: Seated Hip Internal Rotation

execution.note: 10-25 reps per side, ideally performed morning and evening.

instructions: Step 1: Sit on the floor with your legs wide in a 'V' shape.
Step 2: Lean back slightly on your hands for support.
Step 3: Rotate one knee inward toward the floor, aiming for a 90-degree angle at the knee.
Step 4: Keep the other leg stable and the opposite hip grounded.
Step 5: Return to center and alternate sides.

variations.name: Deep Squat Internal Rotation
variations.instruction_note: Perform the rotation while staying in a deep squat position for added intensity.

variations.name: 90/90 Lift
variations.instruction_note: A strength-based variation where you lift the hip from a 90/90 seated position.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Do not force the knee to the floor if you feel sharp pain. Only rotate within your comfortable range of motion.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp knee or hip joint pain.

enrichment.benefits: Increases the space in the lower pelvis (outlet), which is critical for the baby's exit during delivery.

name: Frog Pose Rocking

execution.note: Move rhythmically to help baby descend.

instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours and widen your knees as far as comfortable.
Step 2: Turn your toes outward so your inner feet are flat on the floor.
Step 3: Keep your forearms or hands on the floor for support.
Step 4: Slowly rock your hips back toward your heels and then forward again.

variations.name: Skeletal View Alignment
variations.instruction_note: Focus on the backward rock to specifically open the sit bones.

variations.name: Deep Hip Opening Hold
variations.instruction_note: A static version for deeper release of the pelvic floor.

variations.name: Quick Prep Variation
variations.instruction_note: Perform 8 rhythmic rocks as part of a high-efficiency circuit.

variations.name: Frogger Stretch
variations.instruction_note: Really focus on opening the hips wide to the sides.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Use a blanket under your knees if the floor is too hard. Skip or narrow your knees if you feel sharp pain in the pubic bone (SPD).
safety_profile.contraindications: Severe Symphysis Pubis Dysfunction (SPD).

enrichment.benefits: Creates space in the upper pelvis for the baby to drop down and engage.

name: Deep Squat (Malasana)

execution.note: Hold the bottom position to maximize the stretch.

instructions: Step 1: Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width apart, toes turned out.
Step 2: Lower your hips down toward the floor into a deep squat.
Step 3: Keep your heels on the floor and your chest lifted.
Step 4: Place your elbows inside your knees to gently press them open.
Step 5: Rock gently side-to-side to find ease in the hips.

variations.name: 3-Minute Endurance Hold
variations.instruction_note: A static hold designed to build the mental and physical stamina needed for active labor.

variations.name: Casual Shifting (Daily Life)
variations.instruction_note: Perform this weight shift casually throughout the day, such as while brushing your teeth.

variations.name: Deep Squat to Hamstring Stretch
variations.instruction_note: From the squat, lift your hips toward the ceiling while keeping hands low to stretch the hamstrings.

variations.name: Low Squat Rocks
variations.instruction_note: Perform 10 rhythmic rocks in the deepest part of the squat to relax the pelvic floor.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: If your heels lift, place a rolled-up mat or towel under them. Use a yoga block for support if you have hemorrhoids or pelvic heaviness.
safety_profile.contraindications: Avoid deep unsupported squats if you have a known history of cervical insufficiency.

enrichment.benefits: Builds leg strength, stretches the inner thighs, and prepares the pelvic floor for the pressure of delivery.

name: Bear Hover

execution.note: Work up to holding for 60 seconds total.

instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours with toes tucked under.
Step 2: Take a big inhale to expand the belly.
Step 3: On the exhale, 'hug the baby' in and up towards your spine.
Step 4: Keeping that core engagement, lift your knees just 1 inch off the floor.
Step 5: Hold while maintaining a flat, table-top back.

variations.name: 3-Second Pulse Lift
variations.instruction_note: Instead of a long hold, perform repeated 3-second lifts with a full breath between each.

variations.name: Alternating Shoulder Tap
variations.instruction_note: While hovering, tap the opposite shoulder with your hand to increase stability challenge.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: This is an advanced move. Ensure you are 'hugging the baby' effectively to avoid straining the lower back.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop immediately if you see 'coning' (a ridge forming down the center of your abs) or feel excessive pelvic pressure.

enrichment.benefits: Builds significant core and shoulder stability to help manage the weight of the third-trimester belly.

name: Asymmetric Rock Back

execution.note: Perform 10 rocks on each side.

instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours.
Step 2: Place one knee on a yoga block or a thick book to elevate it.
Step 3: Keep your hands flat on the floor for stability.
Step 4: Slowly rock your hips back toward your heels and then forward again.
Step 5: Complete the set on one side, then switch the block to the other knee.

variations.name: Lizard Pose Deepen
variations.instruction_note: A more intense version of asymmetrical hip opening using a deep lunge position.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Ensure the block is stable before putting weight on it. If this causes sharp pain in the front of the pelvis, stop and move to a symmetrical rock.
safety_profile.contraindications: Severe Symphysis Pubis Dysfunction (SPD) where uneven leg height causes pain.

enrichment.benefits: Uses an uneven pelvic position to help 'untwist' uterine ligaments and encourage the baby into an optimal head-down position.

name: Thoracic Reach & Rotate

execution.note: Perform 10 reaches per side.

instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours.
Step 2: Place one hand behind your head or reach it toward the ceiling.
Step 3: Rotate your chest and elbow/hand toward the ceiling.
Step 4: Rotate back down, tucking the moving arm under your chest toward the opposite side.
Step 5: Follow your hand with your eyes to ensure the movement comes from the upper back.

variations.name: Kneeling Lunge Rotation
variations.instruction_note: Perform the rotation while in a kneeling lunge position to add a hip flexor stretch.

variations.name: Low Lunge Thoracic Reach
variations.instruction_note: A dynamic version focused on reaching the arm high to maximize ribcage expansion.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Avoid over-twisting the lower back; keep the focus on the upper spine and shoulders. If you feel dizzy, perform the movement more slowly or switch to a seated version.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp pain in the spine or ribs.

enrichment.benefits: Reduces upper back tension and increases the capacity of the ribcage to expand, helping with third-trimester shortness of breath.

name: Butterfly Pose (Rocking/Pulses)

execution.note: Stay upright to maintain space for the baby.

instructions: Step 1: Sit on the floor with the soles of your feet touching and knees out to the sides.
Step 2: Pull your feet as close to your body as is comfortable for your belly.
Step 3: Hold your ankles or feet and sit up tall.
Step 4: Gently rock your torso side-to-side or pulse your knees up and down.

variations.name: Butterfly Pulses
variations.instruction_note: Gently bounce the knees up and down like butterfly wings to loosen the hip sockets.

variations.name: Active Knee Press
variations.instruction_note: Use your hands or elbows to gently apply downward pressure on the knees for a deeper stretch.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: If sitting on the floor is uncomfortable, sit on a yoga block or a folded blanket to tilt the pelvis forward. Avoid leaning back too far.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp inner thigh or groin pain.

enrichment.benefits: Increases blood flow to the pelvic region and helps release the adductors, which can become tight as the body prepares for labor.

name: Quadruped Hip Shift

execution.note: Perform 15-20 repetitions per side.

instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours with a neutral spine.
Step 2: Place one knee on a yoga block or a thick book to elevate it.
Step 3: Keep your hands and the opposite foot planted for stability.
Step 4: Lift the non-elevated hip toward the ceiling, then lower it toward the floor.
Step 5: Focus on the movement coming from the pelvis and hip, not the spine.

variations.name: Standing Hip Shift
variations.instruction_note: A standing version where you shift weight side-to-side in a forward fold to achieve similar pelvic mobility.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Maintain a steady breath and avoid any sudden, jerky movements. Ensure the block is secure on your mat.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop if you feel sharp pain in the pubic bone or have been diagnosed with severe Symphysis Pubis Dysfunction (SPD).

enrichment.benefits: Improves internal rotation of the hip, which helps open the pelvic outlet and supports the baby's descent during the second stage of labor.

name: Lizard Pose

execution.note: Hold for 30-45 seconds per side.

instructions: Step 1: Start in a low lunge with your back knee on the floor.
Step 2: Place both hands on the floor inside your front foot.
Step 3: Walk your front foot out toward the edge of the mat to make room for your belly.
Step 4: Keep your chest lifted and gently sink your hips forward and down.
Step 5: For more intensity, you can lower onto your forearms if space allows.

variations.name: Lizard with Hip Circles
variations.instruction_note: Add small, slow circles with the hips while in the pose to increase joint mobility.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Use yoga blocks under your hands if the floor feels too far away. Ensure the back knee is padded with a blanket.
safety_profile.contraindications: Avoid if you feel pulling or sharp pain in the pubic symphysis.

enrichment.benefits: Deeply opens the hips and stretches the psoas, which helps balance the pelvis for baby's positioning.

name: Side Knee to Chest

execution.note: Perform 10 slow, controlled repetitions on each side.

instructions: Step 1: Lie on your side with your legs stacked and a slight bend in your knees.
Step 2: Support your head with your bottom arm or a pillow.
Step 3: Gently pull your top knee toward your chest, using your hand to guide it.
Step 4: Hold for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the leg back down.
Step 5: Roll onto the other side and repeat the sequence.

variations.name: Side-Lying Thoracic Rotation
variations.instruction_note: While holding the knee-to-chest position, rotate your upper body away from the knee to add a spinal twist.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Use a pillow between your knees if stacking them causes hip discomfort. Ensure you are not rolling onto your back.
safety_profile.contraindications: None.

enrichment.benefits: Relieves lower back tension and creates space in the upper pelvis to help the baby move into a better position.

name: Kneeling Side Plank

execution.note: Hold for 30 seconds per side.

instructions: Step 1: Prop yourself up on your forearm with your elbow stacked directly under your shoulder.
Step 2: Keep your bottom knee bent on the floor and your top leg extended or stacked.
Step 3: On an exhale, 'hug the baby' in and up to engage the core.
Step 4: Lift your hips from the bottom waist to create a straight line from head to knees.
Step 5: Hold while breathing into your ribs and belly.

variations.name: Side Plank Inhale/Exhale
variations.instruction_note: Inhale to lower slightly and expand the ribs, exhale to lift and 'hug' the baby in.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Avoid letting your hips sag, which can strain the lower back. If this feels too intense, keep your hips on the floor and focus on the 'hug' engagement.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop if you notice coning/doming in the center of the abdomen or feel sharp pubic bone pain.

enrichment.benefits: Strengthens the lateral core muscles, which helps manage the shifting center of gravity and reduces back pain.

name: Goddess (Sumo) Squat

execution.note: Focus on keeping the spine vertical to allow space for the belly.

instructions: Step 1: Stand with your feet wide, heels in and toes pointed out.
Step 2: Lower your hips down, ensuring your knees stay tracked over your toes and don't collapse inward.
Step 3: Keep your chest lifted and shoulders stacked over your hips.
Step 4: Press through your heels to return to a standing position.

variations.name: Dynamic Goddess Pulses
variations.instruction_note: Perform small, rhythmic pulses at the bottom of the squat to build endurance and simulate labor rhythms.

variations.name: Goddess with Side Stretch
variations.instruction_note: Hold the squat and reach one arm overhead at a time to expand the ribcage and side body.

variations.name: Uneven (Block) Squat
variations.instruction_note: Place one foot on a block while squatting to shift the pelvis and address asymmetry.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Do not go deeper than your current mobility allows; your center of gravity is shifting. Use a wall or chair for balance if you feel unsteady.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop if you feel sharp pelvic pressure or pulling in the pubic symphysis.

enrichment.benefits: Builds the quad and glute strength necessary for standing labor positions and opens the inner thighs.

name: 90/90 Hip Lift

execution.note: Perform 10 controlled lifts per side.

instructions: Step 1: Sit on the floor with your front leg at a 90-degree angle and your back leg at a 90-degree angle.
Step 2: Keep your spine tall and place your hands on your hips or the floor for balance.
Step 3: Drive through your front shin and back knee to lift your hips off the floor into a kneeling position.
Step 4: Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control.
Step 5: Switch leg orientation and repeat on the other side.

variations.name: 90/90 Static Stretch
variations.instruction_note: Hold the seated 90/90 position without the lift to focus purely on the deep hip rotation.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: The belly may make the forward lean difficult; stay upright to maintain space. Use your hands on the floor to assist the lift if needed.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp knee pain or sacroiliac (SI) joint instability.

enrichment.benefits: Strengthens the gluteus medius and improves hip internal and external rotation, which is vital for pelvic mobility during birth.

name: Kneeling Psoas Stretch

execution.note: Hold for 45 seconds per side.

instructions: Step 1: Start in a kneeling position with one foot forward and the back knee on a padded surface.
Step 2: Gently tuck your tailbone under (posterior pelvic tilt) to engage the stretch.
Step 3: Lean forward slightly until you feel a stretch in the front of your back hip.
Step 4: Keep your chest lifted and avoid arching your lower back.
Step 5: Reach the arm on the stretching side up toward the ceiling for a deeper release.

variations.name: Dynamic Hip Rocking
variations.instruction_note: Slowly rock in and out of the stretch to help the pelvic ligaments adjust.

variations.name: Psoas with Side Lean
variations.instruction_note: Lean your torso toward the front-leg side while reaching up to lengthen the entire side-body.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Use a wall or chair for balance as your center of gravity shifts. Ensure the back knee is well-padded.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp pain in the groin or sacroiliac (SI) joint.

enrichment.benefits: Releases tension in the psoas and iliacus, allowing the pelvis to tilt properly for baby's engagement.

name: Supported Kneeling Lunge

execution.note: Hold for 60 seconds per side.

instructions: Step 1: Place a large exercise ball in front of you.
Step 2: Step one foot forward into a lunge and drop your back knee to a padded floor.
Step 3: Lean your torso forward to rest your forearms and chest on the ball.
Step 4: Allow your hips to sink forward while the ball supports your upper body weight.
Step 5: Breathe deeply into your lower back and pelvis.

variations.name: Lunge with Hip Circles
variations.instruction_note: While leaning on the ball, move your hips in small, gentle circles to lubricate the hip socket.

variations.name: Deep Lunge Rocking
variations.instruction_note: Drive the hips forward and back rhythmically to increase mobility.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: The ball is excellent for taking the weight off your spine as the belly grows. Ensure the ball is not on a slippery surface.
safety_profile.contraindications: None.

enrichment.benefits: Provides a safe way to stretch the psoas and hip flexors while minimizing the risk of falling due to 3rd-trimester balance shifts.

name: Pelvic Clock Circles

execution.note: Perform 10 full rotations in each direction.

instructions: Step 1: Start on hands and knees in a neutral tabletop position.
Step 2: Imagine your pelvis is a clock face parallel to the floor.
Step 3: Move your hips in a slow, smooth circle, hitting every 'hour' on the clock.
Step 4: Focus on the sensation of the hip sockets and lower back loosening up.
Step 5: Switch directions after 10 full rotations.

variations.name: Large Hip Swings
variations.instruction_note: Increase the diameter of the circles to involve the side body and ribs.

variations.name: Ball Pelvic Circles
variations.instruction_note: Perform identical circular movements while seated on a birthing ball to use gravity.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: If circling causes any 'clicking' or 'popping' in the pubic bone, reduce the size of the circles.
safety_profile.contraindications: None.

enrichment.benefits: Reduces stiffness in the SI joints and helps the baby navigate the pelvic mid-plane.

name: Standing Hip Shifts

execution.note: Perform 20 shifts total (10 per side).

instructions: Step 1: Stand with your feet slightly wider than hip-width apart.
Step 2: Keep a soft bend in your knees; do not lock them.
Step 3: Shift your weight and your hips slowly to the left.
Step 4: Shift your weight and your hips slowly to the right.
Step 5: Keep your torso upright and your hands on your hips to feel the movement in the pelvic bowl.

variations.name: Standing Pelvic Tilts
variations.instruction_note: While standing, perform forward and backward tilts of the pelvis instead of lateral shifts.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: A great alternative if kneeling on the floor is uncomfortable. Use a wall or counter for balance if needed.
safety_profile.contraindications: None.

enrichment.benefits: Loosens the soft tissues around the hips and encourages the baby to find an optimal position by providing gentle movement.

name: Bird Dog

execution.note: Perform 12 reps per side.

instructions: Step 1: Start on hands and knees with a flat back and core engaged.
Step 2: On an exhale, 'hug the baby' and simultaneously extend the opposite arm and opposite leg.
Step 3: Keep your hips level to the floor; do not let the lifting hip rotate upward.
Step 4: Hold for a second at the top, then slowly lower back to the starting position.
Step 5: Alternate sides or complete all reps on one side before switching.

variations.name: Static Core Hold
variations.instruction_note: Hold the extended position for 5-10 seconds to increase the stability challenge.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Do not lift the leg higher than hip height to avoid arching the lower back. Focus on length rather than height.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop if you feel sharp lower back pain or notice abdominal coning.

enrichment.benefits: Improves balance and counteracts the forward pull of the belly by strengthening the back extensors.

name: Kneeling Side Crunch

execution.note: Perform 10 slow, controlled crunches per side.

instructions: Step 1: Start in a kneeling side plank position, supported by your bottom knee and forearm.
Step 2: Extend your top arm overhead and your top leg out straight.
Step 3: On an exhale, 'hug the baby' and bring your top elbow and top knee together toward your side.
Step 4: Inhale as you extend back out to the starting position.
Step 5: Maintain a stable torso; do not let your hips sag toward the floor.

variations.name: Standing Side Reach
variations.instruction_note: A lower-intensity standing version that focuses on the side-body stretch rather than the crunch.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: The range of motion may be smaller due to the belly; focus on the muscle contraction rather than touching the elbow to the knee.
safety_profile.contraindications: Stop if you notice coning/doming or feel sharp pulling in the round ligaments.

enrichment.benefits: Improves lateral core strength and hip stability, which can help alleviate common third-trimester side-body and hip pain.

name: Seated Hip Wipers

execution.note: 10 slow repetitions per side.

instructions: Step 1: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, wider than hip-width.
Step 2: Place your hands behind you for support and lean back slightly.
Step 3: Slowly drop both knees to the left toward the floor.
Step 4: Bring them back to center and then drop both knees to the right.
Step 5: Keep your sit bones relatively grounded to maximize the internal rotation of the hip.

variations.name: 90/90 Flow
variations.instruction_note: Transition directly into a 90/90 position at the end of the 'wipe' for a deeper stretch.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: If the belly feels in the way, lean back further on your hands or widen your stance. Only go as far as your comfortable range of motion allows.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp knee pain or sacroiliac (SI) joint discomfort.

enrichment.benefits: Improves the mobility of the hip capsule and creates functional space in the lower pelvis for the baby to descend.

name: Single-Leg Happy Baby

execution.note: Hold for 45 seconds per side.

instructions: Step 1: Lie on your back (use a wedge or pillows to stay slightly upright if lying flat is uncomfortable).
Step 2: Bend one knee toward your chest and then out toward your armpit.
Step 3: Reach for your shin, ankle, or the outer edge of your foot with your hand.
Step 4: Keep the other leg relaxed, either flat on the floor or with the foot planted and knee bent.
Step 5: Gently pull the knee toward the floor while keeping the sole of the foot facing the ceiling.

variations.name: Side-Lying Happy Baby
variations.instruction_note: If lying on your back is not an option, perform this while lying on your side, pulling the top knee toward your shoulder.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Avoid holding this pose for long periods on your back to prevent compression of the vena cava; 45 seconds is generally safe for most, but listen to your body.
safety_profile.contraindications: Dizziness or shortness of breath when lying on your back.

enrichment.benefits: Provides a deep, asymmetrical stretch to the pelvic floor and helps loosen the adductors, creating a 'path of least resistance' for the baby.

name: Yoga Ball Pelvic Circles

execution.note: Perform 20 slow circles in each direction.

instructions: Step 1: Sit centered on a properly inflated birthing ball with feet flat and wide for stability.
Step 2: Rest your hands on your knees or hips.
Step 3: Move your pelvis in a slow, circular motion as if you are drawing a circle with your tailbone.
Step 4: Keep your upper body relatively still, letting the movement come from the hips and lower back.
Step 5: Focus on making the circles smooth and hitting all edges of the ball's surface.

variations.name: Figure-8 Sway
variations.instruction_note: Instead of circles, move your hips in a horizontal figure-8 pattern to further mobilize the SI joints.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Ensure the ball is the correct size (your knees should be slightly lower than your hips). Wear grippy socks or be on a non-slip mat.
safety_profile.contraindications: None.

enrichment.benefits: Reduces lower back pressure and uses the 'pelvic rocking' motion to encourage the baby into an anterior (front-facing) position.

name: Poppy Pose

execution.note: Stay here for 2 minutes to let gravity do the work.

instructions: Step 1: Start on all fours.
Step 2: Keep your hips stacked directly over your knees (do not sit back on your heels).
Step 3: Walk your hands forward until your forehead or chest rests on the floor or a pillow.
Step 4: Keep your 'bum' high in the air to create an incline for the baby.
Step 5: Breathe deeply into your belly, allowing it to hang heavy.

variations.name: Chest-Supported Poppy
variations.instruction_note: Place a stack of pillows under your chest if you have shoulder tightness or acid reflux.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: If you feel lightheaded, come out of the pose slowly. Ensure your knees are wide enough to accommodate your belly.
safety_profile.contraindications: None.

enrichment.benefits: Specifically opens the pelvic inlet (the top) to help a baby who is high up or 'sunny-side up' find a better angle.

name: Polar Bear (Ball Support)

execution.note: Stay for 3 minutes to allow deep relaxation of the uterine ligaments.

instructions: Step 1: Kneel on a soft surface with a large exercise ball in front of you.
Step 2: Drape your chest and arms over the ball, keeping your hips high and knees wide.
Step 3: Rest your head on your arms or the ball.
Step 4: Gently rock the ball side-to-side or forward-and-back to shift the pelvis.
Step 5: Breathe deeply into your belly, letting it hang completely.

variations.name: Static Polar Bear
variations.instruction_note: A stillness-focused version used for deep relaxation before bed.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: If you experience heartburn, use more pillows or a larger ball to keep your head slightly higher than your stomach.
safety_profile.contraindications: None.

enrichment.benefits: Uses gravity and gentle motion to help the baby move out of the pelvis just enough to rotate into the optimal head-down, front-facing position.

name: Single-Leg Box Squat

execution.note: Focus on a slow descent and a powerful upward press.

instructions: Step 1: Stand in front of a stable chair or bench.
Step 2: Extend one leg slightly forward, keeping most of your weight on the standing leg.
Step 3: Inhale and slowly lower your hips toward the chair while keeping your chest lifted.
Step 4: Once your glutes tap the chair, exhale, 'hug the baby,' and press through your heel to stand up.
Step 5: Complete the set on one side before switching.

variations.name: Supported Box Squat
variations.instruction_note: Hold onto a wall or a stable counter if you feel unsteady during the descent.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Avoid locking your knees at the top of the movement. Ensure your chair is against a wall so it cannot slide.
safety_profile.contraindications: Sharp knee pain or severe pelvic girdle pain (PGP).

enrichment.benefits: Builds the leg endurance needed for active birth positions and stabilizes the pelvis.

name: Figure-8 Sway

execution.note: Complete 15 full '8' patterns.

instructions: Step 1: Sit on the birthing ball with feet wide and flat for a stable base.
Step 2: Imagine drawing an '8' or an infinity symbol with your tailbone on the ball.
Step 3: Move your hips diagonally forward to the left, then loop around and move diagonally forward to the right.
Step 4: Keep your shoulders relaxed and your chest open.
Step 5: Let the movement be fluid and hypnotic—great for labor prep.

variations.name: Side-to-Side Sway
variations.instruction_note: A simpler lateral movement if the figure-8 feels too complex.

safety_profile.trimester_3_notes: Maintain your balance by keeping your gaze forward rather than down at your hips.
safety_profile.contraindications: None.

enrichment.benefits: Deeply loosens the sacroiliac (SI) joints and encourages the baby to descend and rotate through the middle of the birth canal.
